text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : Neopentane forms only one monosubstituted derivative.

Statement (II) : Melting point of neopentane is higher than n-pentane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Neopentane, $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{4}$, has four identical $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ groups on one quaternary carbon, so all twelve hydrogens are equivalent and monohalogenation gives only one product, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{X}$. Statement I is correct.

Melting point depends on how well the molecules pack in the crystal. The nearly spherical, highly symmetrical neopentane packs much better than the zig-zag n-pentane, so its melting point is far higher: neopentane $-16.6{}^{\circ }\text{C}$, n-pentane $-129.8{}^{\circ }\text{C}$. Statement II is correct.


[IMG]

Branching lowers the boiling point (neopentane $9.5{}^{\circ }\text{C}$, n-pentane $36.1{}^{\circ }\text{C}$) because of the smaller surface area, but for melting point molecular symmetry decides.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

Electronic configuration of four elements A, B, C and D are given below :

(B) $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{4}$

(C) $1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{5}$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

text: A tetrapeptide, " $x$ " on complete hydrolysis produced glycine (Gly), alanine (Ala), valine (Val), leucine (Leu) in equimolar proportion each. The number of tetrapeptides (sequences) possible involving each of these amino acids is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the number of tetrapeptide sequences possible using the amino acids glycine (Gly), alanine (Ala), valine (Val), and leucine (Leu), we consider the concept of permutations. Since each tetrapeptide sequence consists of four different amino acids, we need to calculate the number of ways to arrange these four different elements.

The formula for the number of permutations of a set of $n$ distinct elements is given by $n!$ (n factorial), where $n!=n\times (n-1)\times (n-2)\times \cdots \times 1$.

For our case:

$n=4$

Hence, the number of possible sequences (or permutations) is:

$4!=4\times 3\times 2\times 1=24$

Thus, there are 24 different tetrapeptide sequences possible using each of the four amino acids exactly once.

text: In 3,3-dimethylhex-1-en-4-yne, there are $_________$ $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$, $_________$ $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ and $_________ sp$ hybridised carbon atoms respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
3,3-Dimethylhex-1-en-4-yne is $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (C-1 to C-6 along the main chain, two methyl groups on C-3).


[IMG]

C-1 and C-2 form the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ double bond: 2 $sp^{2}$ carbons.

C-4 and C-5 form the $\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{C}$ triple bond: 2 $sp$ carbons.

C-3 (four single bonds), C-6 and the two methyl carbons on C-3 form only single bonds: 4 $sp^{3}$ carbons.

So the numbers of $sp^{3}$, $sp^{2}$ and $sp$ carbons are 4, 2 and 2 respectively.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.5 gram of an organic compound gave 60 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound (Aqueous tension at $300\mathrm{K}=15\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg}$ $) is___________$%.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the percentage composition of nitrogen using Dumas' method, follow these calculations:

Calculate the Pressure of Nitrogen Gas:

$\text{Pressure of}\mathrm{N}_{2}=(715\text{mmHg}-15\text{mmHg})=700\text{mmHg}$

Calculate the Moles of Nitrogen ($\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}$):

$\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{RT}}$

Where:

$P=700\text{mmHg}$

$V=60\times 10^{-3}\text{L}$

$R=0.0821\text{L atm/mol K}$

$T=300\text{K}$

Plug the values into the equation:

$\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}=\frac{700\times 60\times 10^{-3}}{760\times 0.0821\times 300}\approx 2.24\times 10^{-3}\text{mol}$

Calculate the Mass of Nitrogen Gas:

$\text{Mass of}\mathrm{N}_{2}=2.24\times 10^{-3}\text{mol}\times 28\text{g/mol}=0.06272\text{g}$

Determine the Percentage Composition of Nitrogen:

$%\mathrm{N}_{2}=\left (\frac{0.06272}{0.5}\right )\times 100\approx 12.57%$

Thus, the percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is approximately 12.57%.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text:
Which of the following statements are true?

(A) The subsidiary quantum number $l$ describes the shape of the orbital occupied by the electron.

(B) 
[IMG]
 is the boundary surface diagram of the $2\mathrm{p}_{x}$ orbital.

(C) The + and - signs in the wave function of the $2p_{x}$ orbital refer to charge.

(D) The wave function of $2\mathrm{p}_{x}$ orbital is zero everywhere in the $xy$ plane.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) The subsidiary (azimuthal) quantum number $l$ defines the three-dimensional shape of the orbital: $l=0$ spherical (s), $l=1$ dumbbell (p), and so on. (A) is true.

(B) The boundary surface of $2p_{x}$ consists of two lobes along the $x$-axis on opposite sides of the nucleus, which is what the figure shows. (B) is true.


[IMG]

(C) The + and − signs on the lobes give the sign (phase) of the wave function, not electric charge. (C) is false.

(D) $\Psi _{2p_{x}}$ is proportional to $x$, so it is zero only where $x=0$, i.e. in the $yz$ plane (the nodal plane). In the $xy$ plane it is non-zero everywhere except along the $y$-axis, so (D) is false.

Only (A) and (B) are true.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Arrange the following in order of magnitude of work done by the system/on the system at constant temperature.

(a) $\left |w_{\text{reversible}}\right |$ for expansion in infinite stages.

(b) $\left |w_{\text{irreversible}}\right |$ for expansion in single stage.

(c) $\left |\mathrm{w}_{\text{reversible}}\right |$ for compression in infinite stages.

(d) $\left |w_{\text{irreversible}}\right |$ for compression in single stage.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Consider an isothermal change of an ideal gas between state 1 $(P_{1},V_{1})$ and state 2 $(P_{2},V_{2})$ with $V_{2}>V_{1}$ and $P_{1}>P_{2}$. The magnitude of work is the area under the $P_{\text{ext}}$–$V$ path.

Reversible path (infinite stages): $P_{\text{ext}}\approx P$ at every step, so expansion and compression follow the same isotherm and

$|w_{\text{rev}}|=nRT\ln \dfrac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}$

for both, so a = c.

Single-stage expansion: the gas expands against the final pressure $P_{2}$, so $|w|=P_{2}(V_{2}-V_{1})$, a rectangle lying under the isotherm. Hence b  c.

Therefore, d > c = a > b.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text:
When a concentrated solution of sulphanilic acid and 1-naphthylamine is treated with nitrous acid $(273\mathrm{K})$ and acidified with acetic acid, the mass $(\mathrm{g})$ of 0.1 mole of product formed is :

(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{H}:1,\mathrm{C}:12,\mathrm{N}:14,\mathrm{O}:16,\mathrm{S}:32$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Nitrous acid at 273 K diazotises sulphanilic acid to the 4-sulphobenzenediazonium ion, $\mathrm{HO}{}_{3}\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$.

In acetic acid this diazonium ion couples with 1-naphthylamine at C-4 (para to $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$), giving the red azo dye 4-[(4-amino-1-naphthyl)azo]benzenesulphonic acid:

$\mathrm{HO}{}_{3}\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{10}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$

Its formula is $\mathrm{C}{}_{16}\mathrm{H}{}_{13}\mathrm{N}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}\mathrm{S}$: C $=6+10=16$, H $=1+4+6+2=13$, N $=3$, O $=3$, S $=1$.

Molar mass $=16(12)+13(1)+3(14)+3(16)+32=192+13+42+48+32=327\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

Mass of 0.1 mol $=0.1\times 327=32.7\text{g}\approx 33\text{g}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of thermodynamic properties of Haber's process?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Haber's process is $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})2\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}(\mathrm{g})$, with $\Delta _{r}H^{θ}\approx -92\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (exothermic) and $\Delta _{r}S^{θ}\approx -199\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ (gaseous moles fall from 4 to 2).

$\Delta _{r}H^{θ}$ and $\Delta _{r}S^{θ}$ are both negative and almost independent of temperature, so each is a nearly flat line below zero.

$-\Delta _{r}H^{θ}/T$ is positive and decreases as $T$ rises.

$-\dfrac{\Delta _{r}G^{θ}}{T}=-\dfrac{\Delta _{r}H^{θ}}{T}+\Delta _{r}S^{θ}=R\ln K$

So this curve lies a constant $|\Delta _{r}S^{θ}|$ below the $-\Delta _{r}H^{θ}/T$ curve, decreases with $T$ and becomes negative at high temperature, as $K$ falls for the exothermic reaction.

Graph (A) shows all four of these curves; in (B) the quantities $\Delta _{r}H^{θ}/T$ and $\Delta _{r}S^{θ}/T$ are drawn flat though they vary as $1/T$, in (C) $-\Delta _{r}H^{θ}/T$ turns negative, and in (D) $\Delta _{r}S^{θ}$ is positive.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text:
Reactant A converts to product D through the given mechanism (with the net evolution of heat):
  A → B     slow;     ΔH = +ve
  B → C     fast;     ΔH = -ve
  C → D     fast;     ΔH = -ve
  Which of the following represents the above reaction mechanism?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The profile must show: A → B over the highest barrier (slow) with B above A ($\Delta H>0$); C below B and D below C (both later steps exothermic) over small barriers (fast); and D below A, since heat is evolved overall.

Profile (A): C lies above B, so step B → C is endothermic, and D lies above A, so the overall reaction is endothermic.

Profile (B): D lies above A, so the overall reaction is endothermic; the step C → D also has a very large barrier, so it would not be fast.

Profile (C): C lies above B, so step B → C is endothermic.

Profile (D): A rises to B over the largest barrier, B → C and C → D each go downhill over small barriers, and D lies below A, so every condition is met.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text: The nature of oxide $(\mathrm{TeO}_{2})$ and hydride $(\mathrm{TeH}_{2})$ formed by Te , respectively are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Down group 16 the stability of the +6 state decreases (inert pair effect), so the reducing power of the dioxides falls from $\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}$ to $\mathrm{TeO}{}_{2}$: $\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}$ is easily oxidised to the +6 state and acts as a reducing agent, while $\mathrm{TeO}{}_{2}$ resists oxidation and acts as an oxidising agent.

The H–E bond enthalpy decreases from $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ to $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{Te}$, so the hydrides release $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ more easily down the group and $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{Te}$ is the most acidic hydride of the group.

Thus $\mathrm{TeO}{}_{2}$ is oxidising and $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{Te}$ is acidic.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
' $x$ ' g of NaCl is added to water in a beaker with a lid. The temperature of the system is raised from $1^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. Which out of the following plots, is best suited for the change in the molarity $(\mathrm{M})$ of the solution with respect to temperature ?

[Consider the solubility of NaCl remains unchanged over the temperature range]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When $x$ grams of NaCl are added to water in a beaker and the temperature is increased from $1^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, the molarity of the solution changes due to the volumetric changes of water. 

Temperature from $1^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $4^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$:  

Water is densest at $4^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$.

As the temperature increases from $1^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $4^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, the water volume decreases due to increased density.

This decrease in volume results in an increase in molarity because molarity is inversely proportional to the solution's volume.

Temperature from $4^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$:  

Beyond $4^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, water expands with an increase in temperature.

Therefore, as temperature rises to $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, the volume of the water increases.

The dilution leads to a decrease in molarity, since molarity is inversely proportional to volume.

Thus, the molarity first increases as temperature rises to $4^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, but then decreases as it continues to $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. The graphical representation of this relationship would exhibit an initial increase in molarity, followed by a decrease, correlating with changes in the volume of water due to temperature variations.

text: The type of hybridization and the magnetic property of $[\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}$ are,
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Determine the oxidation state of manganese in $[\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}:$  

Chloride (Cl⁻) has a charge of -1.  

With six chloride ions, the total charge contributed by the ligands is $6(-1)=-6.$  

Let the oxidation state of Mn be $x.$ Then:  

$x-6=-3⟹x=+3.$  

So, manganese is in the +3 oxidation state.

Find the d-electron count for Mn(III):  

The neutral manganese atom has the electronic configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{2}.$  

Removing three electrons (first from the 4s, then from the 3d) gives:  

$\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}:[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{4}.$  

Therefore, Mn(III) is a $d^{4}$ system.

Predict the spin state in an octahedral complex:  

Chloride (Cl⁻) is a weak-field ligand, meaning it produces a relatively small crystal field splitting ($\Delta _{o}$).  

When $\Delta _{o}$ is small, the pairing energy is higher than $\Delta _{o},$ so electrons prefer to remain unpaired.  

For a $d^{4}$ configuration in a high-spin octahedral complex, the electrons will be distributed as:  

Three electrons in the three $t_{2g}$ orbitals (one in each)  

One electron in one of the $e_{g}$ orbitals  

This results in a total of 4 unpaired electrons, making the complex paramagnetic.

Determine the type of hybridization:  

In octahedral complexes, the two common hybridizations are:  

$d^{2}sp^{3}$ (inner orbital complex), typically seen in low-spin complexes where inner 3d orbitals are available because the electrons are paired.  

$sp^{3}d^{2}$ (outer orbital complex), seen in high-spin complexes where the inner $3d$ orbitals are occupied by unpaired electrons.  

Since $[\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}$ is high-spin (because of Cl⁻ being a weak-field ligand), the inner 3d orbitals are not available for hybridization.  

Therefore, the complex uses the outer orbitals (the 4s, 4p, and 4d orbitals), leading to an $sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridization.

Conclusion:  

The hybridization of $[\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}$ is $sp^{3}d^{2}.$  

It is paramagnetic with four unpaired electrons.

Thus, the correct answer is:

Option A: $sp^{3}d^{2}$, paramagnetic with four unpaired electrons.

    (IV)

$\text{Choose the correct answer from the options given below :}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The correct matching is:

(A) Simple distillation → (III) Chloroform + Aniline  

(B) Fractional distillation → (I) Diesel + Petrol  

(C) Distillation under reduced pressure → (IV) Glycerol + Spent-lye  

(D) Steam distillation → (II) Aniline + Water  

So the answer is Option A.

Brief rationale:

Simple distillation (A):  

• $bp(\text{CHCl}_{3})=61^{\circ }\text{C},bp(\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{NH}_{2})=184^{\circ }\text{C}$  

• Δbp is large, so the lower-boiling chloroform distils off cleanly.

Fractional distillation (B):  

• Petrol (40–200°C) and diesel (180–360°C) have overlapping but distinct boiling-range cuts.  

• A fractionating column resolves them efficiently.

Vacuum distillation (C):  

• Glycerol boils ≈290°C at 1 atm—too high for normal distillation.  

• Lowering the pressure brings its boiling point down, letting you separate it from the spent-lye.

Steam distillation (D):  

• Aniline (bp≈184°C) can be co-distilled with water around 98°C, avoiding thermal decomposition and separating it from the aqueous phase.

text: The d-orbital electronic configuration of the complex among $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{3}]^{3+},[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}$, $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ and $[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ that has the highest CFSE is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Identify the oxidation state and d-electron count for each complex:

For $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{3}]^{3+}$:

Ethylenediamine (en) is neutral.

Oxidation state of cobalt is +3.

Cobalt (atomic number 27) in the +3 state gives a $d^{6}$ configuration.

With strong/moderate field ligands like en, the complex is low spin, leading to a configuration of $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$.

For $[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}$:

Each fluoride ion is $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ so, with six of them, Co must be in the +3 state again.

However, since fluoride is a weak field ligand, this complex adopts a high spin configuration for $d^{6}$, resulting in $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$.

For $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$:

Water is neutral.

Manganese in the +2 state gives a $d^{5}$ configuration.

With weak field water, the $d^{5}$ configuration is high spin: $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$.

For $[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$:

Zinc in the +2 state has a $d^{10}$ configuration.

In an octahedral field, all 10 electrons fill the orbitals as $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{4}$.

Calculate the crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) for each case:

The CFSE in an octahedral field can be estimated as:

$\mathrm{CFSE}=(n_{t_{2g}}\times -0.4\Delta _{o})+(n_{e_{g}}\times 0.6\Delta _{o})$

For $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$ (low-spin $d^{6}$ in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{3}]^{3+}$):

$\mathrm{CFSE}=6(-0.4\Delta _{o})+0(0.6\Delta _{o})=-2.4\Delta _{o}$

For $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$ (high-spin $d^{6}$ in $[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}$):

$\mathrm{CFSE}=4(-0.4\Delta _{o})+2(0.6\Delta _{o})=-1.6\Delta _{o}+1.2\Delta _{o}=-0.4\Delta _{o}$

For $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ (high-spin $d^{5}$ in $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$):

$\mathrm{CFSE}=3(-0.4\Delta _{o})+2(0.6\Delta _{o})=-1.2\Delta _{o}+1.2\Delta _{o}=0$

For $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{4}$ (for $d^{10}$ in $[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$):

$\mathrm{CFSE}=6(-0.4\Delta _{o})+4(0.6\Delta _{o})=-2.4\Delta _{o}+2.4\Delta _{o}=0$

Compare the CFSE values:

$t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$ gives a CFSE of $-2.4\Delta _{o}$ (most negative, hence highest stabilization).

The others result in less stabilization (or net zero).

Conclusion:

The complex with the highest CFSE is the one with the configuration $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, which corresponds to $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_{3}]^{3+}$.

Thus, the answer is:

Option A: $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text:
For the reaction $\mathrm{A}\to \mathrm{B}$ the following graph was obtained. The time required (in seconds) for the concentration of A to reduce to $2.5\mathrm{g}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ (if the initial concentration of A was $50\mathrm{g}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ ) is [MATH$_$FAILED] . (Nearest integer)

Given : $\log 2=0.3010$


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the graph, [A] falls from 40 to $20\text{g L}^{-1}$ between 5 s and 15 s, and from 20 to $10\text{g L}^{-1}$ between 15 s and 25 s.

A half-life that stays the same as the concentration halves shows first-order kinetics, with $t_{1/2}=10\text{s}$.

For first order, $k=\dfrac{2.303\log 2}{t_{1/2}}$, so

$t=\dfrac{2.303}{k}\log \dfrac{[\text{A}]_{0}}{[\text{A}]}=\dfrac{t_{1/2}}{\log 2}\log \dfrac{50}{2.5}$

$t=\dfrac{10}{0.3010}\times \log 20=\dfrac{10\times 1.3010}{0.3010}=43.2\text{s}$

Hence, the answer is 43.

text:
When 1 g each of compounds AB and $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$ are dissolved in 15 g of water separately, they increased the boiling point of water by 2.7 K and 1.5 K respectively. The atomic mass of A (in amu$) is____________$ $\times 10^{-1}$ (Nearest integer)

(Given : Molal boiling point elevation constant is $0.5\mathrm{K}\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For AB

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}=2.7\mathrm{K} \\ 2.7=1\times 0.5\times \mathrm{m} \\ \mathrm{m}=\dfrac{27}{5} \end{array}$

Let molar mass of $AB=x$.

So $\frac{1/x}{15}\times 1000=\frac{27}{5}$

$x=12.34$

For $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}=1.5\mathrm{K} \\ 1.5=1\times 0.5\times \mathrm{m} \\ \mathrm{m}=3 \end{array}$

Let molar mass of $\mathrm{AB}_{2}=\mathrm{y}$

So $\frac{1/\mathrm{y}}{15}\times 1000=3$

$\begin{array}{l} y=\dfrac{1000}{45} \\ y=22.22 \end{array}$

Now let a and b be atomic masses of A and B respectively, then

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=12.34\text{...... (i)} \\ \mathrm{a}+2\mathrm{b}=22.22\text{...... (ii)} \\ \mathrm{b}=22.22-12.34=9.88 \end{array}$

Now $\mathrm{a}=12.34-9.88=2.46$

$=24.6\times 10^{-1}=25\times 10^{-1}$

text: $0.2%(\mathrm{w}/\mathrm{v})$ solution of NaOH is measured to have resistivity $870.0\mathrm{m}\Omega \mathrm{m}$. The molar conductivity of the solution will $be__________\times 10^{2}\mathrm{mS}\mathrm{dm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Determine the conductivity from the resistivity.  

The resistivity is given as  

$ρ=870.0\text{m}\Omega \cdot \text{m}.$  

Convert this into ohm·meters:  

$870.0\text{m}\Omega \cdot \text{m}=870.0\times 10^{-3}\Omega \cdot \text{m}=0.87\Omega \cdot \text{m}.$

Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity:  

$κ=\frac{1}{ρ}=\frac{1}{0.87}\approx 1.15\text{S/m}.$

Find the concentration of NaOH in mol/m³.  

A $0.2%(\mathrm{w}/\mathrm{v})$ solution means there are 0.2 grams of NaOH per 100 mL of solution.  

In 1 liter (1000 mL) there are:  

$\frac{0.2\text{g}}{100\text{mL}}\times 1000\text{mL}=2\text{g/L}.$

The molar mass of NaOH is approximately $40\quad \text{g/mol}$. Thus, the molarity is:  

$\text{Molarity}=\frac{2\text{g/L}}{40\text{g/mol}}=0.05\text{mol/L}.$

Since $1~\text{L}=0.001\text{m}^{3}$, converting to SI units (mol/m³):  

$c=0.05\text{mol/L}\times \frac{1}{0.001\text{m}^{3}/\text{L}}=50\text{mol/m}^{3}.$

Calculate the molar conductivity in SI units.  

Molar conductivity $\Lambda _{m}$ is given by:  

$\Lambda _{m}=\frac{κ}{c}.$

Substituting the values:  

$\Lambda _{m}=\frac{1.15\text{S/m}}{50\text{mol/m}^{3}}=0.023\text{S}\cdot \text{m}^{2}/\text{mol}.$

Convert the molar conductivity to the desired units (mS dm² mol⁻¹).  

First, convert the conductivity:  

$0.023\text{S}\cdot \text{m}^{2}/\text{mol}\times 1000\frac{\text{mS}}{\text{S}}=23\text{mS}\cdot \text{m}^{2}/\text{mol}.$

Now, convert the area units. Recall that:  

$1~\text{m}^{2}=100\text{dm}^{2}.$  

So,  

$23\quad \text{mS}\cdot \text{m}^{2}/\text{mol}=23\times 100\text{mS}\cdot \text{dm}^{2}/\text{mol}=2300\text{mS}\cdot \text{dm}^{2}/\text{mol}.$

The problem asks for the answer in the form  

$\text{[blank]}\times 10^{2}\text{mS}\cdot \text{dm}^{2}/\text{mol}.$  

Expressing 2300 mS dm²/mol in this form:  

$2300\qquad \text{mS}\cdot \text{dm}^{2}/\text{mol}=23\times 10^{2}\text{mS}\cdot \text{dm}^{2}/\text{mol}.$

Thus, the molar conductivity is  

$23\times 10^{2}\text{mS}\cdot \text{dm}^{2}/\text{mol}.$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

Consider the above sequence of reactions. 151 g of 2-bromopentane is made to react. Yield of major product P is $80%$ whereas Q is $100%$.

Mass of product Q obtained $is________ g$.

(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{H}:1,\mathrm{C}:12,\mathrm{O}:16,\mathrm{Br}:80$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
2-Bromopentane, $\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{11}\mathrm{Br}$, has molar mass $5\times 12+11\times 1+80=151\text{g mol}^{-1}$, so 151 g of it is 1 mol.

Alcoholic KOH brings about dehydrohalogenation; by Saytzeff's rule the major product P is the more substituted alkene, pent-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$. At 80% yield, P formed $=0.8\times 1=0.8$ mol.

Bromine adds across the double bond of P to give Q, 2,3-dibromopentane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CHBrCHBrCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ ($\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$), molar mass $5\times 12+10\times 1+2\times 80=230\text{g mol}^{-1}$.


[IMG]

At 100% yield, Q formed = 0.8 mol, so

$\text{Mass of Q}=0.8\times 230=184\text{g}$

Hence, the answer is 184.
